_meta.title: Care/of customer — 'constant traveler'
_meta.why_strong: Specific situational trigger (travel), specific physical pain (six bottles), and the quiz-as-trojan-horse decision pattern that defines personalized DTC. JTBD is operational, not aspirational.

persona.name: Road-warrior Rachel, 34, consultant who hops climates weekly
persona.location_context: NYC home base, travels for work 3 weeks/month, hotels in different climates and time zones, cooks rarely
persona.primary_job: When I'm packing my carry-on at 11pm before a 6am flight and realize I've forgotten which vitamins to bring, I want a routine that's already personalized and pre-portioned, so I can stop being the friend whose immune system collapses every quarter.

pain_points.label: Six bottles is a non-starter for travel
pain_points.description: Lugging 6 supplement bottles in carry-on means TSA scrutiny + weight + half of them get left at home; ends up taking nothing some weeks

pain_points.label: Routine collapses across time zones
pain_points.description: Take supplements 'with breakfast' loses meaning when breakfast was 4 hours ago in another time zone; misses entire days of the regimen

pain_points.label: Decision fatigue at the supplement aisle
pain_points.description: Doesn't want to research each vitamin individually; got overwhelmed at Whole Foods last month and bought nothing

trust_needs: Quiz feels personalized, not algorithmic guess (asks specific questions)
Third-party testing on the supplements (NSF / cGMP)
Easy to skip a month or pause the subscription
Founder story or MD on advisory board
decision_triggers: Quiz on a lunch break — low-effort trial
Personalized recommendations with reasoning ('we recommended X because you said Y')
Friend posted her Care/of pack on Instagram
objections: Are these actually high quality or is the personalization just marketing?
What if I don't want one of the recommendations?
Will this auto-renew at a higher price after the intro?
persona.channel_behavior: Instagram + TikTok primary discovery; will Google '[brand] reviews reddit' before checkout; mobile checkout; reads reviews longer than the product page

verbatim_quotes: I'm constantly hopping time zones and climates, so staying healthy is tough.
I had a shelf full of half-used vitamins I'd forget to take.
Now my daily packs travel with me everywhere — no more lugging around six different bottles.
